chapters.who-is-it: Who's "it"? One word changes the answer
chapters.left-to-right: It reads left to right: at "it" it can't know yet
chapters.outro: Next: Watch It Learn to Write

description:
"The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired." You know "it" is the animal. Change one word, "too wide", and "it" is the street. How does an AI tell?

Attention: every word looks back at the words before it, gives each one a weight (how much it matters), and the weights add up to 1. Everything on screen is the real attention of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on these two sentences, recorded on an RTX 3090.

What the real run showed:
- At "it" the model can't know yet. It reads left to right and "tired"/"wide" hasn't come, so all 1,024 attention heads give "it" exactly the same weights in both sentences.
- The switching happens one word later. In layer 8, head 29, "tired" gives the animal 11.1% (the street 4.0%); "wide" gives the street 68.0% (the animal 0.3%).
- Most heads don't switch: 883 of 1,024. 4 switch clearly, 114 lean the right way a little, 23 lean the wrong way. One head is one small part, not the model's understanding.
- The whole model gets it right: after "...too tired. The one that was too tired was the" its top guess is "animal" (33.4%); with "wide" it's "street" (43.1%).

{chapters}

ML, slowly, episode 4 of 5: one idea per video, slow enough to follow on the first watch. Next: Watch It Learn to Write.

Made with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5): lyrics, the song (AI-generated with ACE-Step 1.5), word alignment, the animation (three.js), the render. Renderer forked from mexicat's p(doom) video (MIT).
